Aegĭăleus (quadrisyl. ), ĕi, m., = Αἰγιαλεύς.
I. Son of Æetes, brother of Medea, commonly called Absyrtus; he was cut to pieces by his sister in her flight, and scattered upon the sea-shore, Pac. ap. Cic. N. D. 3, 19, 48; Just. 43, 3.—
II. Son of Adrastus, one of the Epigoni before Thebes, slain by Laodamas, Hyg. Fab. 71.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
